body.statement: For every sequence in \(\mathcal P_n\), including sequences with \(H\to\infty\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\), and the primitive conditional block-dependence and score-diffuseness conditions yield \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P_P\{(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\le z\mid M,\Omega\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). Consequently, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb P_P\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\mid M,\Omega\}\to1-\alpha\). This is an extension of the balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup Choi--Yuan regime along the serial-dependence and growing-window axes, under a strengthened uniform class. Neither full class contains the other, and the \(q=0,H=1\) reduction is asserted only on the intersection with Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v).
body.justification: Native expansion, feasible curvature correction, finite-lag covariance consistency, and fitted-weight stability yield uniform scalar Wald inference over the strengthened class.
body.gap: The result extends the balanced, fixed-rank, common-start, singleton-subgroup Choi--Yuan regime only along serial-dependence and growing-window axes; the full classes are incomparable, and the one-date reduction holds only on their explicit condition intersection.
body.consumer: The interval supports a scalar reanalysis of the SEC Tick Size Pilot's realized average sustained liquidity effect over the treated cohort and declared post window.
body.proof_tex:
Work under an arbitrary sequence \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), conditionally on \((M,\Omega)\).  The replacement of \(\mathrm{def:model\mbox{-}class}\) makes the conditional sub-Gaussian exponential-moment condition a member property, so the established conditional score central limit theorem is available on the same class.

On \(G\times W\), \(\mathrm{ass:common\mbox{-}start\mbox{-}mask}\) gives \(A_{it}=1\), and \(\mathrm{ass:causal\mbox{-}consistency}\) therefore gives \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=Y_{it}(1)\).  Comparing the definitions of the estimator and the causal target, rather than defining the target through the estimator, gives the exact equality
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau-\tau
 &=\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}
 \left[Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}-\widehat M_{it}
       -\{Y_{it}(1)-M_{it}\}\right]\\
 &=-\frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it}).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
The untreated-factor assumption identifies \(M_{it}\) as the conditional untreated signal component; equation (17) is the required observed-law-to-causal bridge for the declared realized cohort-window contrast.

By \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\),
\[
 \frac1{gH}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})
 =L+Q+R_{\mathrm{agg}}.
\tag{18}
\]
Using \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=\widehat\tau+\widehat B_2\), add and subtract \(B_2\) in (17)--(18) to obtain
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau
 =-L-(Q-B_2)-R_{\mathrm{agg}}+(\widehat B_2-B_2).
\tag{19}
\]
Equations (9)--(15) in the proof of the native-transfer theorem show, under the sharpened envelope that defines \(\mathcal P_n\), that each of the last three terms in (19) is \(o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), uniformly over the class.  Therefore
\[
 \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s).
\tag{20}
\]

For variance consistency, let \(d_{j\cdot}=\widehat w_{j\cdot}-w_{j\cdot}\).  Define the \(T\times T\) banded matrices
\[
 (\Gamma_q)_{uv}=1\{|u-v|\le q\}\gamma(v-u),
 \qquad
 (\widehat\Gamma_q)_{uv}=1\{|u-v|\le q\}\widehat\gamma(v-u).
\tag{21}
\]
The definitions of \(s^2\) and \(\widehat V\) imply
\[
 s^2=\sum_{j=1}^Nw_{j\cdot}^{\top}\Gamma_qw_{j\cdot},
 \qquad
 \widehat V=\sum_{j=1}^N(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot})^{\top}
 \widehat\Gamma_q(w_{j\cdot}+d_{j\cdot}).
\tag{22}
\]
Conditional sub-Gaussianity bounds \(|\gamma(h)|\) uniformly by conditional Cauchy--Schwarz.  Since \(q\) is fixed, the maximum absolute row-sum bound and the definition of \(\Delta_\gamma\) give
\[
 \|\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(1),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le(2q+1)\Delta_\gamma=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{23}
\]
Expanding (22), applying Cauchy--Schwarz in the direct sum of the \(N\) row spaces, and using (23) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\widehat V-s^2|
 &\le \|\widehat\Gamma_q-\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|w\|_F^2
   +2\|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|w\|_F\|d\|_F
   +\|\widehat\Gamma_q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|d\|_F^2.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{24}
\]
The established \(\mathrm{lem:score\mbox{-}diffuseness}\) gives \(\|w\|_F^2=O(s^2)\), while the fitted-weight conclusion of \(\mathrm{thm:native\mbox{-}second\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}transfer}\) gives \(\|d\|_F^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\).  Dividing (24) by the positive quantity \(s^2\), whose lower bound is supplied by \(\mathrm{ass:variance\mbox{-}nondegeneracy}\), proves
\[
 \frac{|\widehat V-s^2|}{s^2}=o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{25}
\]
In particular, \(\widehat V>0\) with probability tending uniformly to one.

By \(\mathrm{lem:uniform\mbox{-}score\mbox{-}clt}\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{26}
\]
Normal symmetry gives the same assertion for \(-L/s\).  Combining (20), (25), and (26) by conditional Slutsky's argument gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|\mathbb P_P\!\left(
 \frac{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau}{\sqrt{\widehat V}}
 \le z\,\middle|\,M,\Omega\right)-\Phi(z)\right|
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{27}
\]
For fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), evaluate (27) at the continuity points \(\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\).  By the definition of \(\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\), this yields
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
 \mathbb P_P\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\mid M,\Omega\}
 \longrightarrow1-\alpha.
\tag{28}
\]

The argument is scalar and allows \(H\to\infty\), but it neither proves event-time bands nor changes the fixed known rank.  The class comparison is also restricted as claimed: Choi--Yuan impose independent cell noise, their stated subgroup-size regime, and separate loading and rate conditions, whereas \(\mathcal P_n\) permits fixed-range serial dependence but imposes balanced dimensions, fixed rank and incoherence, \(g\asymp n\), the common-start mask, and singleton target-local fits.  Hence neither full class contains the other.  On the explicit intersection with Choi--Yuan Conditions (i)--(v), \(q=0\), and \(H=1\), the published-reduction proposition gives the one-date reduction.  This proves the revised comparison sentence without claiming equality or nesting of the two full classes.
